public_rationale: On May 6, 2024, Microsoft CTO Kevin Scott described ongoing internal model development and named MAI, Turing and Phi [e1, e2]. This supports the claim that Microsoft maintained options beyond sole reliance on OpenAI [e1]. GPT-4 still powered Microsoft Copilot that day, so the evidence shows diversification alongside continued use of OpenAI [e3].
limitations: The evidence does not establish Nadella's private confidence in Altman or his motives [e1–e3].
It does not quantify reduced dependence or demonstrate that Microsoft's internal models could replace OpenAI's models [e1–e3].
The PYMNTS report corroborates the date and attribution of Scott's statement; its quotation is not independent evidence of technical capability [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Whether or not Satya Nadella has lost confidence in Sam Altman, Microsoft is hedging against relying on OpenAI.

from_speaker: Maybe Satya has lost confidence in Sam, maybe he hasn’t

our_interpretation: In context, not taking any chances means maintaining alternatives to reliance on OpenAI, rather than eliminating every business risk.
The preceding sentence expressly leaves Nadella's private confidence in Altman undecided.
Assess whether Microsoft had active alternative model-development capacity on May 6, 2024, the latest contemporaneously reportable state.
Diversification is inferred from observable activity; a private motive or explicit admission of hedging is not required.
criteria.support_condition: Microsoft had active internal model development or alternative model suppliers that provided options beyond relying solely on OpenAI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records show exclusive reliance on OpenAI, with the supposed alternatives absent or already abandoned.
